name: Serra de Pàndols – Cota 705 memorial
story: The bare limestone ridge of Pàndols, rising to Punta Alta (Cota 705), was the southern bastion of the Ebro bridgehead. Republican troops, including Líster's 5th Army Corps and the 35th Division with the XV International Brigade, held it through August 1938 against repeated Nationalist assaults supported by massive artillery and air bombardment. Men fought on bare rock where trenches could barely be dug and the dead often could not be buried. Nearby Hill 666 was held by International Brigade units, among them the British and Lincoln battalions. The ridge remained in Republican hands until the general collapse of the bridgehead in the autumn.
see: The 'Cub per la Pau' memorial and plaques near the summit, stone parapets and scraped rifle pits, and a panoramic view over the whole Terra Alta battlefield; a separate plaque marks Hill 666 (41.03300, 0.47585).
plan: Reached by a rough forest track from the Gandesa–Pinell de Brai road, then a short walk; check track conditions and fire-risk closures in summer, and carry water.
